# Power Manager Clock-Domain Crossing Module — Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

This module forms the clock-domain crossing boundary for power-management signals. It transfers control, status, configuration, and event information between a main clock domain and an always-on slow clock domain. It also synchronizes a set of asynchronous or mixed-domain status indications.

The module does not make power-management sequencing decisions. It only moves information across clock domains while preserving the meaning, polarity, and encoding of that information.

## 2. Clock and Reset Behavior

- The module shall operate with two independent clock and reset pairs: one for the fast/main domain and one for the slow/always-on domain.
- Each domain’s reset shall initialize all state associated with that domain to a defined reset state.
- Resetting one domain must not asynchronously force outputs in the other domain to their reset state.
- After reset is released, outputs shall remain at their reset values until a new input value or event propagates to that output.

## 3. Reset-State Requirements

The module shall bring its outputs to known safe values after reset.

For configuration and control outputs, the default state must be consistent with a safe, inactive power-management state:

- Wakeup source enables shall be deasserted.
- Reset source enables shall be deasserted.
- The main power keep-alive control shall be asserted, meaning the main power domain is not requested to power down.
- The I/O clock enable shall be deasserted.
- The core clock enable shall be deasserted.
- The low-power USB clock enable shall be deasserted.
- The active USB clock enable shall be asserted.
- The power-up cause output shall be set to the power-on-reset cause.
- The synchronized flash idle indication shall be asserted after reset.
- Any other synchronized output shall be held at its defined inactive or safe reset value until the corresponding source signal changes and the synchronization process updates it.

## 4. Fast-to-Slow Transfers

### 4.1 General Level and Event Behavior

- Level-type signals from the fast domain shall be transferred to the slow domain such that a constant source value eventually appears at the slow-domain output.
- A change in a source level shall propagate to the destination output while preserving the logical value of the signal.
- Pulse-type events from the fast domain shall be delivered to the slow domain exactly once per source pulse. A single source pulse must not be lost, and it must not create multiple destination pulses.

### 4.2 Configuration Snapshot Transfer

A specific set of fast-domain configuration fields shall be transferred to the slow domain only when a configuration synchronization request is received.

- The configuration fields include:
  - wakeup enables
  - reset enables
  - main power keep-alive control
  - I/O clock enable
  - core clock enable
  - low-power USB clock enable
  - active USB clock enable
- The slow-domain configuration outputs shall not update merely because the fast-domain input values change; they shall update only when a configuration synchronization request occurs.
- When such a request occurs, all configuration outputs in the slow domain shall update as a consistent group. A partial update shall not be observable.
- After the request has been transferred and the configuration outputs have been updated, the module shall produce a completion indication in the fast domain.
- The completion indication shall be generated once for each configuration synchronization request.

### 4.3 Power-Management Status Signals

- The fast-domain power-down request shall be transferred to the slow domain as a level signal.
- The fast-domain power-up acknowledgment shall be transferred to the slow domain as a level signal.
- The peripheral request vector from the fast domain shall be transferred to the slow domain with each bit treated as an independent request line. Bits may be synchronized independently.
- The USB IP clock status from the fast domain shall be transferred to the slow domain.

### 4.4 Analog System Response Vector

The analog system response vector may contain multi-bit values that must not be presented to the slow domain in a partially updated or unstable form.

- The slow-domain version of this vector shall be updated only when the incoming vector is stable.
- If the incoming vector is still changing, the previously synchronized value shall remain on the output.
- After reset, this output shall be held at its defined safe reset value.

## 5. Slow-to-Fast Transfers

### 5.1 General Behavior

- Level-type signals from the slow domain shall be transferred to the fast domain such that a constant source value appears at the fast-domain output.
- Pulse-type events from the slow domain shall be delivered to the fast domain exactly once per source pulse.

### 5.2 Power Management Status Signals

- The slow-domain power-up request shall be transferred to the fast domain as a level signal.
- The slow-domain power-down acknowledgment shall be transferred to the fast domain as a level signal.
- The slow-domain invalid-state indication shall be transferred to the fast domain as a level signal.
- The slow-domain USB IP clock enable shall be transferred to the fast domain as a level signal.
- The slow-domain peripheral request vector shall be transferred to the fast domain with each bit treated as an independent request line.

### 5.3 Power-Up Cause Transfer

The power-up cause value must be transferred from the slow domain to the fast domain using a change-qualified mechanism.

- The slow domain provides a change indicator along with the power-up cause value.
- The fast-domain power-up cause output shall not change unless the change indicator changes state.
- When the indicator change is detected, the current power-up cause value shall be captured and presented in the fast domain.
- The output shall hold that value until the next change event is detected.
- After reset, the output shall be the power-on-reset cause.

## 6. Mixed-Domain Synchronization

### 6.1 Flash Idle Indication

The flash idle indication shall be synchronized to the fast domain.

- The module shall preserve the logical meaning of the input.
- After reset, the synchronized flash idle output shall be asserted.

### 6.2 OTP Response Vector

The OTP response vector shall be synchronized to the fast domain.

- The output shall be all-zero after reset.
- A steady input value shall eventually appear at the output without alteration.

### 6.3 ROM Integrity-Check Completion Indication

The ROM integrity-check completion indication is a multibit encoded value and shall be synchronized to the fast domain.

- The encoded meaning of the value shall be preserved.
- The output shall update only when the incoming encoded value is stable.
- If the incoming value is changing, the previous stable output shall be retained.
- After reset, the output shall be at its defined safe reset state.

## 7. Clear-Request Synchronization

The module shall provide a request/acknowledge mechanism for a clear request crossing from the fast domain to the slow domain.

- A clear request asserted in the fast domain shall cause a clear request to be asserted in the slow domain.
- The request transfer shall not be lost.
- An acknowledgment shall be returned to the fast domain only after the clear request has been presented in the slow domain.
- The fast-domain clear request and the slow-domain clear request shall remain coupled so that the slow-domain request is deasserted after the source request is removed and the synchronization delay has elapsed.
- The acknowledgment mechanism shall not require the slow domain to complete any downstream operation before returning acknowledgment.

## 8. Data Integrity and Independence

- For vectors whose bits represent independent request or status lines, the module shall synchronize each bit independently and shall not require all bits to arrive in the destination domain simultaneously.
- For vectors whose bits together form a related value, the module shall ensure that the destination does not observe an inconsistent combination of old and new bits.
- The module shall not alter the logical value, polarity, or encoding of any transferred signal.
